{"database":{"advisory-count":1380,"last-commit":"99670cfc0bc574433034b75876a4b791ccaa2efb","last-updated":"2026-10-27T11:02:42+01:00"},"lockfile":{"dependency-count":615},"settings":{"target_arch":[],"target_os":[],"severity":null,"ignore":[],"informational_warnings":["unmaintained","unsound","notice"]},"vulnerabilities":{"found":true,"count":9,"list":[{"advisory":{"id":"RUSTSEC-2026-0346","package":"rustls","title":"`Debug` impls for client session values expose TLS secrets","description":"The `Debug` implementations of `Tls12ClientSessionValue` and
`Tls13ClientSessionValue` were derived, and so included the TLS 1.2 master
secret or TLS 1.3 resumption PSK in their output.

Custom `ClientSessionStore` implementations that format these values with
`Debug` (for example, when logging) could disclose these secrets to readers of
the logs. This conflicts with rustls's
[key-material redaction policy](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/blob/99f2358cae2954837dbb866faf6727de75489ab9/SECURITY.md#boundary-public-api).

Ordinary connection and built-in session cache `Debug` output is redacted and
is not affected.","date":"2026-10-14","aliases":["GHSA-c8m5-c952-6cm4"],"related":[],"collection":"crates","categories":["crypto-failure"],"keywords":[],"cvss":"CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N","informational":null,"references":[],"source":null,"url":"https://github.com/rustls/rustls/pull/3299","withdrawn":null,"license":"CC0-1.0","expect-deleted":false},"versions":{"patched":[">=0.23.46"],"unaffected":["<0.21.0"]},"affected":null,"package":{"name":"rustls","version":"0.23.45","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index","checksum":"0d41d731c7d2f962d1ccc364cec258de3c0e93b38c2fb3ba97ac74513048d634","dependencies":[{"name":"once_cell","version":"1.21.3","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"ring","version":"0.17.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-pki-types","version":"1.15.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-webpki","version":"0.103.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"subtle","version":"2.6.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"zeroize","version":"1.9.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"}],"replace":null}},{"advisory":{"id":"RUSTSEC-2026-0347","package":"rustls","title":"Buffered application data sent to outer server after ECH rejection","description":"When a server rejects Encrypted Client Hello (ECH), the client completes the
handshake using the outer ClientHello and authenticates the server against the
ECH config's `public_name`. At the end of that handshake, rustls encrypted and
queued any application data buffered via `ClientConnection::writer()` *before*
queueing the `ech_required` alert.

The application correctly receives
`Error::PeerIncompatible(ServerRejectedEncryptedClientHello)`, but the next
`write_tls()` call (needed to send the alert) also sends the buffered
application data. Plaintext meant for the inner server therefore goes to the
client-facing server named by `public_name`.

That server is authenticated, so this is not exploitable by an unauthenticated
party, but it violates RFC 9849 section 6.1.6, which requires the client to
abort with `ech_required` "before sending any application data to the server".

This affects only clients that:

- use `EchMode::Enable` (GREASE ECH is not affected),
- write application data before the handshake completes, and
- connect to a server that rejects their ECH config (for example, because it is stale).

The underlying ordering bug is older, but before 0.23.44 the client checked
the server certificate against the inner server name rather than `public_name`,
so certificate verification failed first and no data was sent.","date":"2026-10-14","aliases":["GHSA-vp88-798v-h67f"],"related":[],"collection":"crates","categories":["crypto-failure"],"keywords":[],"cvss":"CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N","informational":null,"references":[],"source":null,"url":"https://github.com/rustls/rustls/pull/3300","withdrawn":null,"license":"CC0-1.0","expect-deleted":false},"versions":{"patched":[">=0.23.46"],"unaffected":["<0.23.44"]},"affected":null,"package":{"name":"rustls","version":"0.23.45","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index","checksum":"0d41d731c7d2f962d1ccc364cec258de3c0e93b38c2fb3ba97ac74513048d634","dependencies":[{"name":"once_cell","version":"1.21.3","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"ring","version":"0.17.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-pki-types","version":"1.15.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-webpki","version":"0.103.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"subtle","version":"2.6.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"zeroize","version":"1.9.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"}],"replace":null}},{"advisory":{"id":"RUSTSEC-2026-0348","package":"rustls","title":"Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication","description":"The built-in Brotli certificate decompressor (enabled by the non-default
`brotli` crate feature) bounded the size of the decompressed output, but
accepted a peer-selected history window. Brotli's large-window extension was
enabled, so a five-byte header could cause an allocation of 1 GiB. A peer can
abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request.

No trusted certificate is required by the attacker. Affected configurations are:

- clients that enable the `brotli` feature and connect to a malicious server, and
- servers that enable the `brotli` feature and request client certificates.

Applications that do not enable the `brotli` feature are not affected.","date":"2026-10-14","aliases":["GHSA-h2v8-394m-p7vv"],"related":[],"collection":"crates","categories":["denial-of-service"],"keywords":[],"cvss":"CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L","informational":null,"references":[],"source":null,"url":"https://github.com/rustls/rustls/pull/3297","withdrawn":null,"license":"CC0-1.0","expect-deleted":false},"versions":{"patched":[">=0.23.46"],"unaffected":["<0.23.9"]},"affected":null,"package":{"name":"rustls","version":"0.23.45","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index","checksum":"0d41d731c7d2f962d1ccc364cec258de3c0e93b38c2fb3ba97ac74513048d634","dependencies":[{"name":"once_cell","version":"1.21.3","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"ring","version":"0.17.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-pki-types","version":"1.15.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-webpki","version":"0.103.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"subtle","version":"2.6.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"zeroize","version":"1.9.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"}],"replace":null}},{"advisory":{"id":"RUSTSEC-2026-0349","package":"rustls","title":"Unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange","description":"The client recorded the server-selected key exchange group for each server
name when processing the ServerHello, before the server was authenticated.
This record is used to predict which key share to send in future ClientHellos
to that server name.

A network attacker can answer one connection attempt with a ServerHello
selecting X25519, and then close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that
name carry only an X25519 key share, while `supported_groups` still lists
X25519MLKEM768 first. If the genuine server accepts that share rather than
sending a HelloRetryRequest for its preferred hybrid group, the handshake
completes with classical-only key exchange and no error. This persists for as
long as the entry stays in the client's session store.

The impact is loss of post-quantum confidentiality for affected connections
("harvest now, decrypt later"). There is no key compromise and no
authentication bypass.

The following are not affected:

- connections to servers which send a HelloRetryRequest for their preferred group,
- clients with resumption disabled (as nothing is stored), and
- other server names.

This behaviour is discussed in
[draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-tls-key-share-prediction-01.html#name-security-considerations),
so the practical impact depends largely on server policy.","date":"2026-10-14","aliases":["GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28"],"related":[],"collection":"crates","categories":["crypto-failure"],"keywords":[],"cvss":"CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N","informational":null,"references":[],"source":null,"url":"https://github.com/rustls/rustls/pull/3355","withdrawn":null,"license":"CC0-1.0","expect-deleted":false},"versions":{"patched":[">=0.23.46"],"unaffected":[]},"affected":null,"package":{"name":"rustls","version":"0.23.45","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index","checksum":"0d41d731c7d2f962d1ccc364cec258de3c0e93b38c2fb3ba97ac74513048d634","dependencies":[{"name":"once_cell","version":"1.21.3","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"ring","version":"0.17.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-pki-types","version":"1.15.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"rustls-webpki","version":"0.103.14","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"subtle","version":"2.6.1","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"},{"name":"zeroize","version":"1.9.0","source":"registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"}],"replace":null}},{"advisory":{"id":"RUSTSEC-2026-0382","package":"rustls-webpki","title":"Certificate verification may accept distrusted intermediates","description":"Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign

Affected versions may accept certificate paths containing distrusted emSign
